The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies for leading environmental initiatives, promoting employee well-being, and contributing to society. Under the HKMA's overall organizational risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and examined both actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA's office has incorporated multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. Additionally, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only its offices but also its communication and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that employees are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also continuously monitors the transition risks it faces by tracking the greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage associated with its operations. The HKMA's latest climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 related to its own operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) methodology. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol to measure and report its emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from gasoline-powered vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's primary greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect emissions resulting from the consumption of fossil fuels for electricity generation. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA has adopted a conservative approach to estimate major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills, as well as employee air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are provided in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and baseline of this verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" appended to this report. The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to comply with. As a first step toward green commuting, the HKMA began replacing its gasoline-powered vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve full green commuting. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects carried out in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and decorative materials or traded in old items for discounts on new ones to reduce waste. To improve overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in its offices and data centers. In 2024, it upgraded its data center facilities with a modular design for the uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system, further optimizing the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its data center, which is certified under the "BEAM Plus" scheme. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency under partial load conditions, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA has strengthened internal virtual collaboration through digital workspaces, streamlined workflows, and effectively reduced paper usage. Additionally, the HKMA has extended the lifespan of mobile and desktop devices by following manufacturers' software update cycles, thereby prolonging the safe operational life of these devices. To reduce office waste, the HKMA adheres to the "4R" principle—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help develop targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins for different materials at multiple convenient locations throughout its offices. To increase recycling rates, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit net bags in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending its food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Commitment" campaign, pledging to take measures to reduce waste generated from its various activities. The HKMA continues to prioritize the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List," particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages employees to plan their trips carefully, such as by combining multiple journeys when attending overseas events. At the organizational level, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. Additionally, the HKMA participates in the "Gold Standard"-certified carbon offset program to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this program focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA organized various learning activities for employees, such as lectures and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on April 22, 2024, through the entire month of May, the HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month," themed "Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Working." This initiative provided a valuable opportunity for the HKMA to demonstrate its commitment and drive in promoting environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The event included a "Sustainable Development BINGO Scorecard" to encourage employees to adopt green lifestyles, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and a "Kokedama" (Japanese moss ball) indoor plant care workshop; it also featured the sharing of waste audit results and best recycling practices presented by a community recycling center operator. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," the HKMA launched a six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting the importance of responsible waste disposal and reminding employees that small changes in individual habits can significantly improve the organization's overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the release of the "Green Action" video, in which several senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to encourage employees to take action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted an employee survey to assess their understanding of sustainability and gather feedback on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help inform the development of future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as a key driver of change and is committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition, encouraging the financial industry and society at large to adopt sustainable operational practices. The HKMA has introduced several measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the "Shared Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's services in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility (SVF) operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The purpose of expanding the platform's services is to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures introduced in 2024 include SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA questionnaires through a simplified submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system that provides users with a central platform featuring advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper usage, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), and GHG emissions from air travel for 2024, as well as their respective intensities. In addition, the Data also include Scope 3 GHG emissions for 2023 and 2024 arising from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), and employee commuting, together with their respective intensities. The HKMA's GHG emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol"), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covered a total of six office and warehouse premises, comprising five offices located at 1) International Finance Centre Two, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) One World Trade Centre, as well as a warehouse at 6) Lok Shing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the HKQAA examined selected representative data and supporting evidence from the six premises. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and reach a conclusion to obtain reasonable assurance. The verification process was conducted in line with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. It tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and it also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, while performing reliability tests. The verification process further included an assessment of the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the data, and the selection of representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA was responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work was conducted with complete independence and impartiality. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: (i) the Data are materially accurate and reliable; and (ii) the HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Sharon Shum, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025
